name: sc-1300
description: Audio Database Technics SC-1300 ¥ 133,000 (around 1969) Commentary As a sister machine of the SC-1300, this stereo system combines Technics technology as a separate stereo. The SC-1300 uses a multi-amplifier system to improve acoustic characteristics by amplifying the low and mid - to high-frequency ranges with a dedicated power amplifier, while a horn type unit is used for the mid - to high-frequency range to ensure rich musical quality. In the multi-amplifier system, each amplifier is directly connected to a speaker, so that intermodulation distortion and damping factor can be improved and sound quality degradation can be eliminated. Receiver section A quasi complimentary service circuit is adopted for the circuit system of the power amplifier section, and silicon transistors are used on the whole surface to improve mid - and long-range characteristics. Also, by adopting the ITL-OTL-OCL system, we succeeded in completely connecting the amplifier and speaker directly for the first time as a multi-stereo system. This improves low-frequency distortion and degradation of frequency and damping characteristics caused by the output capacitor. A newly developed low-noise IC for the technics separation is used in the first stage of the preamplifier section to enable low-noise reproduction. The preamp section controls the channel level control and listening control. The listening control can be adjusted in two ways : the damping control (for the low range) and the brilliance control (for the high range). The damping control can control the frequency and damping characteristics of the low range by changing the feedback capacitance of the NF. The brilliance control uses a Darlington circuit with C and R, and acts as a filter to increase the brightness of the high range and to cut out the high range noise caused by the program source.
